clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old man presented with decreased vision in his right eye and characteristic retinal lesions. Initial ophthalmologic exam revealed round pigmented chorioretinal lesions with vitreous turbidity. Aqueous humor tested positive for Toxoplasma DNA and IgG/IgM antibodies, and serum was positive for Toxoplasma IgG. He was treated with oral prednisone and azithromycin. Within 7 days, the lesion size was stable, no anterior chamber inflammation was noted, and at 3 months, visual acuity normalized with resolving edema and retinal scarring. Serologies were negative for other infectious agents including HIV, Herpes, Varicella, CMV, and syphilis (VDRL-RPR), supporting exclusion of mimics.
